newsitem.title: FINLAND: Enso in talks to buy German paper maker. [CORRECTED 07:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Enso in talks to buy German paper maker. [CORRECTED 07:55 GMT]

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy in a statement on Friday confirmed it was in talks about buying German newsprint and magazine paper maker E.Holtzmann & Cie. AG.
"At the present time there is nothing to report regarding the progress of the talks or their possible outcome," Enso said.
Daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Friday that negotiations on the acquisition were in the final stretch. Enso's exclusive right to negotiate for Holzmann would end at the start of May.
The price asked for the German firm was 1.3 billion German marks, or almost four billion Finnish markka, the paper said.

Holtzmann, based in Karlsruhe, has annual net sales of three billion markka (corrects from German marks) and 1,600 employees. Its main owner, with four-fifths of its shares, is publishing group Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung (WAZ), Helsingin Sanomat said.
By acquiring Holtzmann, Enso could boost its annual newsprint production capacity to 1.1 million tonnes.
In 1996, Enso produced 857,000 tonnes of newsprint, according to the company's annual report.
In addition to newsprint, Holtzmann makes uncoated super-calendered (SC) magazine paper, the paper said.
